title: Cap. VI open: Orthodox position set out — election from mere divine good pleasure
pass_a_gloss: Chapter VI. The Orthodox position is set forth and confirmed. You have received the adversaries' arguments for that election which they fetch from an antecedent act of the human will. It remains that ours now be brought into the midst, which will show that the election or predestination of singular persons to the infallible attainment of eternal life flows from the mere good pleasure of the mercy of God.
pass_b_english: Cap. VI. The orthodox position is set out and confirmed. You have heard the adversaries' arguments for an election they fetch from an antecedent act of the human will. It remains to bring ours forward — showing that election or predestination of singular persons to the infallible attainment of eternal life flows from the mere good pleasure of God's mercy.
source_text: Cap. VI. Orthodoxa sententia exponitur et confirmatur. Accepistis adversariorum argumenta pro illa electione, quam ex antecedaneo voluntatis humanae actu arcessunt. Restat ut nostra jam in medium proferantur, quae electionem sive praedestinationem singularium personarum ad infallibilem consecutionem vitae aeternae, ex mero Dei misericordiae beneplacito dimanare ostendent.
